findings.failure_mode: missing file, permission denied, or unreadable path aborts the entire program instead of returning a typed error
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, Error> and use .map_err(|e| Error::Io(e)) or equivalent typed error; never unwrap I/O

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() panics on invalid digit or out-of-range value
findings.failure_mode: malformed CSV row causes panic instead of returning a typed Parse/Invalid error
findings.fix: use .parse::<u32>().map_err(|_| Error::Parse) and propagate via ?; remove unwrap entirely

findings.problem: parse::<u32>().unwrap() as u16 performs lossy cast: values 65536..=4294967295 silently truncate to u16 range
findings.failure_mode: invalid sensor value silently wraps to a wrong value, corrupting data integrity
findings.fix: use u16::try_from(parsed_u32).map_err(|_| Error::OutOfRange) or parse directly as u16 via .parse::<u16>().map_err(...)

findings.problem: parts[0] and parts[1] use unchecked Vec indexing with no bounds check before access
findings.failure_mode: empty line or line with fewer than 2 comma-separated fields panics with index out of bounds
findings.fix: use split_once(',') and match on the two-field result; reject lines with fewer fields as invalid

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) performs I/O inside a parser that should be pure
findings.failure_mode: hidden side effect breaks purity of data transformation; cannot be tested or suppressed without modifying the core; logging leaks into the functional core
findings.fix: remove println! entirely; if logging is needed, push it to the imperative shell at the call site outside load_sensors

findings.problem: parts: Vec<String> = line.split(',').map(|part| part.trim().to_string()).collect() allocates a full Vec of owned Strings for a single comma-separated pair
findings.failure_mode: unnecessary heap allocation per line; splits on every comma (not just first) when the grammar is exactly name,value; wastes memory on empty tail parts
findings.fix: use line.split_once(',').ok_or(...) to get exactly two &str refs without allocation

findings.problem: load_sensors combines file I/O (fs::read_to_string) with parsing and logging in a single function
findings.failure_mode: violates functional core / imperative shell separation; parser cannot be tested in isolation; I/O errors and parse errors are conflated
findings.fix: split into: (1) shell function that reads file and delegates to (2) pure parse_lines(&[str]) -> Result<Vec<Record>, Error>

findings.problem: load_sensors returns Vec<Record> with no Result type; all failure modes (I/O, parse, bounds, overflow) silently panic instead of returning typed errors
findings.failure_mode: caller has no way to distinguish or handle specific failure modes; no error taxonomy exists
findings.fix: declare pub fn load_sensors(path: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, SensorError> with an enum covering Io, Parse, Invalid, and OutOfRange variants

findings.problem: Record.name: String stores an owned copy; if the function consumed from a shared buffer the name could be a &str with appropriate lifetime
findings.failure_mode: minor: unnecessary allocation and copy when the data outlives the parser; not a safety issue
findings.fix: keep String in Record for owned lifetime but avoid creating String in the parser by using split_once to produce &str; use String::from or .into() only at the boundary where ownership is required

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for load_sensors throughput or allocation behavior
no profiler data (flamegraph, perf, or similar) to validate allocation profile of the parser path
no allocation audit: Vec<String> per-line allocations are unmeasured and unbounded
no second-ring validation: no runtime bounds-checking, fuzzing, or property-based tests for malformed CSV input
no command-level error handling evidence: no evidence that the imperative shell maps I/O errors to typed domain errors
residual_risk: static review only; no commands run. The crate has multiple BLOCKER violations including unwrap on I/O and parse, lossy as cast, unchecked indexing, hidden println! I/O in a parser, unnecessary heap allocation, and missing typed error domain. The functional core / imperative shell boundary is entirely absent. Without fixing these, the code will panic on any malformed input or missing file, silently corrupt out-of-range values, and leak logging into the core.
